answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with invitation-tree liability. A new identity enters only through an invitation from an established agent, and the inviter's standing is docked if the invitee commits fraud, with the whole branch pruned. A gale of fake accounts therefore burns the reputation of the accounts that spawned them, and a nebula of throwaway identities collapses once its root is cut. Honest agents climb a terrace of trust only by inviting reliable partners, so mass fakery costs the attacker its own hard-won standing.
